forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West Oxfordshire council detected and prosecuted employee fraud across multiple authorities
news_drafts.lead: West Oxfordshire's audit committee heard that a former council employee was convicted of committing fraud against three local authorities, including West Oxfordshire itself, Tewkesbury Borough Council, and Gloucestershire's shared services company Publica Group. The investigation identified weaknesses in the council's employment contracts, Code of Conduct processes, and monitoring of secondary employment. The council has since acted on all 16 recommendations arising from the case, embedding the improvements into its human resources fraud assurance register, a compliance check adopted in July 2026. The discovery and prosecution demonstrate the council's fraud detection systems working in practice.
news_drafts.paper_title: WODC Audit & Governance Committee Report September 2026

findings.paper_title: WODC Audit & Governance Committee Report September 2026
findings.headline: The council adopted a Grant Management Policy and revised Counter Fraud and Anti-Corruption and Anti-Money Laundering policies in July 2026.
findings.detail: Executive Committee adopted a Grant Management Policy in July 2026 setting out processes for grant management, external funding applications, and scheme development. A revised Counter Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policy and updated Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Policy were also adopted. A supporting Grant Management Toolkit addressing fraud risk and mitigation in grant administration is being reviewed and developed.
findings.matters: Strong policy frameworks for grant management, AML/CFT compliance, and fraud prevention reduce exposure to fraud, financial mismanagement, and regulatory breach—all material to the council's risk profile.
findings.quote: A revised Counter Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policy and an updated Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Policy were adopted by Executive Committee in July 2026.

findings.paper_title: WODC Audit & Governance Committee Report September 2026
findings.headline: A former employee was found guilty of fraud committed against multiple local authorities, demonstrating the council's fraud detection capability.
findings.detail: The CFEU investigated a former council employee who held multiple simultaneous contracts of employment. The employee was found guilty of committing fraud against Tewkesbury Borough Council, South Gloucestershire Council, and Publica Group Ltd. The investigation generated 16 recommendations for control improvements in employment contracts, Code of Conduct processes, and secondary employment monitoring; all 16 recommendations have been actioned and incorporated into the HR fraud assurance register.
findings.matters: Successful detection and investigation of a multi-council fraud scheme indicates effective internal controls and demonstrates the council's ability to identify and remediate control weaknesses.
findings.quote: He was found guilty of committing fraud against Tewkesbury Borough Council, South Gloucestershire Council, and Publica Group Ltd.

findings.paper_title: WODC Audit & Governance Committee Report September 2026
findings.headline: Three fraud risk assurance registers have been completed for Procurement, Human Resources, and Revenues and Benefits, with a Housing register in development.
findings.detail: The CFEU has completed fraud risk assurance registers covering Procurement, Human Resources (Vetting and Recruitment), and Revenues and Benefits. These registers assess compliance, partial compliance, and non-compliance against national and local emerging fraud risks. A Housing register is currently in development. Rather than traditional risk scoring, the registers provide an evidence-based compliance assessment for governance officers.
findings.matters: Systematic fraud risk assessments in high-value service areas (procurement, payroll, benefits, housing) reduce vulnerability to fraud losses and demonstrate proactive financial risk management.
findings.figures: Three registers completed; one in development
findings.quote: Work has now been completed in relation to three fraud risk assurance registers relating to Procurement, Human Resources (Vetting and Recruitment), and Revenues and Benefits. A Housing register is in development.

findings.paper_title: WODC Audit & Governance Committee Report September 2026
findings.headline: The council was inspected on investigatory powers compliance and confirmed fully compliant by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner's Office.
findings.detail: The Council was inspected in summer 2026 by the Investigatory Powers Commissioner's Office regarding compliance with RIPA 2000 and IPA 2016. The Commissioner confirmed full compliance based on written responses to the Inspector's letter, providing independent assurance of the council's governance controls.
findings.matters: Full compliance with investigatory powers legislation demonstrates the council has strong internal control frameworks and risk governance in place, which is material to credit assessment.
findings.figures: Inspection in summer 2026; full compliance confirmed
findings.quote: The Commissioner has confirmed that the responses provided to the Inspector's letter provided assurance that the Council was fully compliant.

findings.headline: Capital programme carries £4.4m slippage from 2025/26 with extended delivery timelines on temporary accommodation
findings.detail: Against an approved £13.46m capital programme, Q1 spend was only £1.064m. Slippage includes £4.4m from 2025/26 (waste vehicles, building repairs, temporary accommodation). Additional risk: three of eight emergency accommodation properties are not scheduled for occupation until Q2 2027/28.
findings.matters: Significant slippage (32% of programme) indicates execution challenges; extended timelines for temporary accommodation tie up capital longer than planned and suggest procurement or specification delays
findings.figures: £13.46m approved capital programme, £1.064m Q1 spend, £4.4m slippage
findings.quote: At the end of Q1 capital expenditure is £1.064m against an approved Capital Programme for the year of £13.46m, which includes slippage from 2025/26 of £4.4m related to Waste Vehicle replacement, repairs to our buildings and renovation of the newly acquired temporary accommodation properties
